newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller sees chance of early elections.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller sees chance of early elections.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said on Wednesday early polls were on top of Turkey's agenda amid a rift in the ruling coalition over Islamist activism.
"An agenda with elections at the top of it has emerged. The solution is with the people," she told a meeting of her True Path Party MPs.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's government has slowly been crumbling since the army began pushing it to crack down on Islamist activism in February.

The True Path is to debate pulling out of the government coalition at a series of meetings in the coming days. "Our party's bodies will meet in the days ahead and everything will become clear," Ciller said.
"Whatever we do, let's do it together."
The media said Ciller would ask the party for the authority to demand that Erbakan hand over power to her soon to take the country to early elections. Polls are due by 2000.
Erbakan and Ciller, also the foreign minister, are due to swop jobs next year under a power-sharing deal.
But Ciller argues she can deflect the army's wrath from the government if she takes over as prime minister earlier and promises elections next spring.

The secularist generals have declared their fight against Islamists to be a matter of "life or death" for Turkey. Their pressure has forced three True Path ministers and a handful of MPs to quit the party in the last month.

The government now has a parliamentary majority on paper of just one but vacant seats give it a larger margin. It needs a simple majority in parliament to call early elections, favoured by some of the opposition.
